title: Anyone here uses Unreal Engine? What is your workflow?
author: FutureLynx_
selftext:
I made some small prototypes using JS/TS and phaser using AI, and its very fast and convenient.

And since then I postponed my Unreal projects indefinitely. 

I really want to finish my Unreal projects, but when i think about the workflow, it makes me really hesitate, because of how much friction Blueprints have with AI.

Even if I convert all the Blueprints to C++. The editor will still get in the way. And the compiles, and reopening of the editor will slow down a lot.

Another bad thing, is the data tables and data assets, that I use for everything. 

While using AI with Phaser, it can read everything and edit everything directly. So lets say you have your list of units, and you want to increase the price or the hp of all units by 20%.

In Unreal you would have to export the data table to CSV. Then tell AI to edit the CSV. And then reimport.

For the last days I have been thinking about this a lot.

Should I attempt to finish my last Unreal Project (its been going on for 1 year), and will take maybe another 4 months to finish properly. I think if I have done with AI right now, it could take less to do it from scratch, but it wouldn't have a lot of the optimizations that I made in Unreal.

comments.author: Xijamk
comments.body: Have you tried ue-mcp.com?, it's really great for unreal, way better that the basic official mcp from epic.

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body: looks nice though it doesnt seem to support ue4.27. My projects are all 4.27. thanks though.

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body: I tried it already. I prefer the old version. Its more minimalistic, less baggage.

replies.author: DoggoDadagon
replies.body: I mean at that point just go with godot, if you're using unreal trust me you want to update if for nothing else just the AI toolsets in 5.8. We're about to get unreal 6, and you'll want the AI perks that it's shipping with, might as well make the update easy.

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body: I understand but i've been told to update since UE 5.0. And i never felt the need. Plus i was always hearing about others who went back to UE4.27, or issues they were facing with UE5. By UE5.3 i tested and still felt like it was a downgrade. Exactly no reason to update when we are about to have UE6 without blueprints and probably better AI support.

replies.author: DoggoDadagon
replies.body:
Yeah but updating directly from 4 to 6 will be a pain, it's best to update one version at a time. 5.3 was probably the worst version of 5. IMO 4.27 wasn't that great, there's not really any reason to use it, people went back to it because they were mad about the perf of 5 without realizing you can just disable lumen, nanite, VSMs etc and just do it the old school way.

But I'm just trying to be helpful, you do you, if you like 4 then by all means ship with it.

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body:
Yeah so I always felt like 4 had everything i needed. And everything 5 has I dont need it. On top of that most of my projects were started in 4. So I stayed in 4.

When UE6 comes out, I'll take a look, and if it has good AI support, and drops the blueprints, then ill go for it. Hopefully is less bloated than UE5. UE5 was iirc 80 GB. UE4 is 40 GB.

comments.author: egonosz
comments.body:
Why you need to reopen editor when you compile, that should be needed only if you edit engine or editor code?

I am 100% sure unreal has tools which can import expert csc you can ask your agent to write a script what it will use to export import it.

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body: Everytime you change c++ code you need to compile. You can hot reload, but its risky if you are doing anything in the headers / constructor.

replies.author: egonosz
replies.body:
How many times you change the Ctor? I guess if you go full c++ you will need it to change it more times, but you can change header functions which not using ue reflection, so that would not be that bad with full cpp, I guess.

Do you use the ai agent as support for small changes or you make it to do big features?

replies.author: FutureLynx_
replies.body: It is not recommended to touch anything in the header files, that includes function signatures too. So all you can do is just change stuff inside a function. I'm always changing stuff in the header files. Other than that, I often need to debug. And that requires launching from visual studio. 90% of the times im closing the editor. How many times do you change something in code that is only inside a function. Hot reload is not a reliable alternative.
